subject: A premium 3D anatomical model of a leg as a dark translucent silhouette on a near-black field, seen from a high three-quarter angle, the knee bent above a step, the foot about to land on the step below, only the patellar tendon legible inside it. Exactly as in the start frame.

camera.movement: Locked off on a small tripod: the camera does not move at all, no pan, no tilt, no push, no drift.

motion: Already stepping down on the first frame: the leg comes DOWN the stair — the foot lowers from the upper step and lands flat on the step below while the knee bends deeper to catch the body's weight, the whole leg visibly travelling downward within the frame; as the foot lands the spot at the patellar tendon immediately below the kneecap flares brighter, then eases back, staying one tight spot. One step down in about two seconds. Everything in frame keeps the exact form, proportion and count it has in the start frame, first frame to last — nothing melts, merges, splits, grows or becomes something else. One small movement, completing inside the clip, subject fully in frame throughout, nothing leaving frame and returning. quadriceps, hamstrings and calf shortens and thickens as the load arrives, the patellar tendon visibly tightens and straightens along its length, and the whole structure compresses a few degrees. The anatomy takes the weight — it is not a still model with light played over it.
lighting: Capture characteristics exactly as in the start frame — same tone-mapping, same noise, same colour temperature. No grading change across the clip.
